introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2, subject code 0575. Time allowed: two and a half hours.

Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three.

Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory to all candidates, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions; if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions).

All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Les valeurs retenues donnent un point d'intersection a coordonnees entieres (1, -2) verifie sur les deux droites, ce qui confirme la lecture. Points imprimes 5 + 3 = 8, conformes.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given the lines $l_1$ and $l_2$ whose vector equations are:

$l_1:\ \mathbf{r}=-2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+\lambda(3\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})$

$l_2:\ \mathbf{r}=3\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+\mu(2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})$, where $\lambda$ and $\mu$ are constants.

Find:

(i) the position vector of the point of intersection of $l_1$ and $l_2$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the point of intersection the two position vectors are equal.

$$
(-2+3\lambda)\mathbf{i}+(3-5\lambda)\mathbf{j}=(3+2\mu)\mathbf{i}+(-1+\mu)\mathbf{j}
$$

Equate the coefficients:

$$
\mathbf{i}:\ -2+3\lambda=3+2\mu\qquad(1)
$$

$$
\mathbf{j}:\ 3-5\lambda=-1+\mu\qquad(2)
$$

From (2): $\mu=4-5\lambda$. Substitute into (1):

$$
-2+3\lambda=3+2(4-5\lambda)=11-10\lambda\ \Rightarrow\ 13\lambda=13\ \Rightarrow\ \lambda=1,\quad \mu=4-5=-1
$$

Position vector: with $\lambda=1$ in $l_1$: $-2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}=\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$.

Check with $l_2$ and $\mu=-1$: $3\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}=\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$. Same point.

**The point of intersection has position vector $\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}$, i.e. the point $(1,-2)$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) the cosine of the angle between $l_1$ and $l_2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The angle between two lines is the angle between their direction vectors:

$\mathbf{d}_1=3\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{d}_2=2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}$.

$$
\mathbf{d}_1\cdot\mathbf{d}_2=3(2)+(-5)(1)=1,\qquad |\mathbf{d}_1|=\sqrt{9+25}=\sqrt{34},\qquad |\mathbf{d}_2|=\sqrt{4+1}=\sqrt5
$$

$$
\cos\theta=\frac{\mathbf{d}_1\cdot\mathbf{d}_2}{|\mathbf{d}_1||\mathbf{d}_2|}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{34}\sqrt5}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{170}}\approx0.0767
$$

**$\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{170}}\approx0.077$** (so $\theta\approx85.6^\circ$).
